findings.title: Checkout error summary takes focus every time the error count changes, so the next Tab or click lands on the summary and typed characters are lost
findings.route: /porudzbina (step 1 Kontakt; same component on every step, e.g. step 4 terms)
findings.context: 1440x900 Chromium, guest, keyboard and mouse, consent answered. The code path does not depend on width. The 390 rerun timed out on the shared server.
steps: Add /deo/kocioni-disk-prednji-276-24-mm-demo-0004 to the cart and open /porudzbina
Leave every field empty and press Enter on „Dalje“: the error summary „Proverite 4 polja“ gets focus (expected)
Focus „Ime“, type „Petar“ and press Tab
Expected focus: „Prezime“. Actual: focus jumps back to the summary („Proverite 3 polja“), and anything typed next goes nowhere
Mouse: click into „Prezime“, type, then click into „Telefon“. Focus is pulled to the summary again („Proverite 2 polja“) and the digits typed are lost
findings.expected: The summary gets focus once per submit attempt (DESIGN-SYSTEM §9.2: „the form-level error summary receives focus on submit“). Fixing a field and moving on keeps focus where the user put it.
findings.actual: The summary takes focus on every change in the number of errors, including blur revalidation. Keyboard and mouse users are thrown back up after each correction and lose input. Measured twice (earlier run and a rerun at 21:50): after Tab from the corrected Ime, focus was div[role=alert] and co-lastName stayed empty. After clicking Telefon, focus was div[role=alert] and co-phone stayed empty.
findings.suggested_fix: In components/checkout/CheckoutForm.tsx ErrorSummary, stop keying focus on list.length. Pass an `attempt` counter that nextStep()/submit increment only when validation fails, and focus the summary in an effect keyed on that counter. Blur and change revalidation must never move focus. Add an e2e step: after an empty submit, fix Ime, press Tab, expect focus on #co-lastName.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order, SC 3.2.2 On Input; DESIGN-SYSTEM §9.2 and §12.1 rule 7; BRIEF §9 (WCAG 2.2 AA, full keyboard use)

verification.notes:
I reproduced this with my own script on the shared :3100 build. Before that I looked for reasons it might not be a defect and found none. No DECISIONS entry allows focus to move on revalidation. DESIGN-SYSTEM (line 654) and ARCHITECTURE (line 287) both say the summary "receives focus on submit". MECHANICS.md MP-02 already fixed the same class of problem in the registration form, which now gates the summary on submitCount. InquiryForm and MechanicRegistrationForm focus the summary only on submit. Only CheckoutForm.tsx:129-131 keys focus on list.length. The form uses mode "onTouched", so every blur, and every keystroke in a field that was already blurred, can change the error count and pull focus back to the summary. A control run with no errors behaves normally (Tab goes Ime -> Prezime -> Telefon), so this is not a harness artefact.

findings.title: Vehicle picker, cart drawer and header search do not return focus to the control that opened them: focus drops to <body>
findings.route: Every storefront page with the header or the hero picker, e.g. /, /deo/kocioni-disk-prednji-276-24-mm-demo-0004, /delovi/kocioni-diskovi
findings.context: 1440x900 and 390x844 Chromium, keyboard only, consent answered
steps: On /, focus „Izaberite vozilo“ (header chip at 1440 or hero trigger at 390), press Enter, then press Escape (or Tab to „Zatvori“ and press Enter). Check document.activeElement
On the product page, press Enter on „Dodaj u korpu“, focus the header „Korpa, 1 artikal“, press Enter (the drawer opens), then press Escape
At 390 on /delovi/kocioni-diskovi, press Enter on „Pretraga delova“, type „disk“, then press Escape
findings.expected: On close, focus returns to the invoking control, as it already does for the mobile menu (→ „Otvori meni“) and the filter sheet (→ „Filteri“).
findings.actual: Vehicle picker: 8/8 combinations (1440/390 × header/hero trigger × Escape/Zatvori) leave focus on BODY. Cart drawer: BODY after Escape at 1440 and 390. Search sheet at 390: BODY after Escape. Keyboard and screen-reader users are sent back to the top of the document after every vehicle choice or cart peek.
evidence: docs/qa/audit/a11y-store/states-menu-filters-vehicle390.json (menu and filter sheet return focus correctly)
findings.suggested_fix: Root cause: these overlays are controlled via `open` from global state with no Radix Trigger (components/vehicle/VehiclePickerDialog.tsx:271/277, components/cart/CartDrawer.tsx:45, components/shell/HeaderSearch.tsx:55), so Radix has no trigger to refocus. MobileNav passes `trigger` and works. In components/ui/Dialog.tsx and components/ui/Sheet.tsx, when no `trigger` prop is given, store document.activeElement when the overlay opens. In onCloseAutoFocus, call preventDefault() and focus the stored element if it is still connected, otherwise #sadrzaj. Add an e2e check for all three overlays.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order; DESIGN-SYSTEM §12.1 rule 5 („Esc closes overlays; focus returns to the trigger“); BRIEF §9 full keyboard use

findings.title: Expired or revoked session turns every account area into a blank white page (HTTP 200 with a Location header and an empty body)
findings.context: Any viewport and browser (seen in Chromium at 390 and 1440). State: browser still holds __convexAuthJWT + __convexAuthRefreshToken cookies but the refresh token is no longer valid (30-day session lapsed, signed out on another device, password reset, staff account removed).
steps: Open a fresh browser context and set cookies __convexAuthJWT=<any expired JWT> and __convexAuthRefreshToken=revoked-or-expired-token for localhost:3100 (or keep an old session until its refresh token lapses).
Open http://localhost:3100/admin (also /nalog or /majstor/brza-porudzbina).
Observe the page, the title and the response.
Reload the page.
findings.expected: A 307 redirect to /prijava?next=/admin with a sign-in form (the same as for a visitor with no cookies, which does get a 307).
findings.actual: The response is HTTP 200 with header location: /prijava?next=%2Fadmin, Set-Cookie clearing the auth cookies, and a 0-byte body. The browser does not follow a Location on a 200, so the user sees a blank white page with an empty <title> (screen readers announce an empty document). Only a manual reload reaches /prijava. Reproduced for /admin, /nalog and /majstor/brza-porudzbina; it also blanked /nalog/porudzbine and /majstor/cenovnik for the audit's own stale sessions.
evidence: docs/qa/audit/a11y-app/verify2.json (staleSession: status 200, location /prijava?next=%2Fadmin, title '', bodyText 0; afterReload /prijava)
docs/qa/audit/a11y-app/verify.json (account: /nalog/porudzbine title '' headings []; cenovnik: title '', axe document-title + html-has-lang)

curl -H 'Cookie: __convexAuthJWT=eyJ...x; __convexAuthRefreshToken=abc123invalid' localhost:3100/admin -> 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK / location: /prijava?next=%2Fadmin', body 0 bytes; without cookies -> 'HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect'
findings.suggested_fix: Root cause is in @convex-dev/auth 0.0.95 convexAuthNextjsMiddleware (node_modules/@convex-dev/auth/dist/nextjs/server/index.js lines 110-114): when refreshTokens is set (including null after a failed refresh) it wraps the handler's response in NextResponse.next(response), which keeps the headers but drops the 307 status. Fix in proxy.ts or with patch-package: when the handler returns a redirect, set/clear the auth cookies on that redirect response and return it (for example, patch the wrapper to `if (response.headers.has('location')) { await setAuthCookies(response, authResult.refreshTokens, cookieConfig); return response; }`), or upgrade @convex-dev/auth if fixed upstream. Add an e2e test: request /admin, /nalog and /majstor with an invalid refresh-token cookie and expect a 307 to /prijava.
findings.standard: BRIEF §9 (sign-in and admin order handling must work; no broken states); WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled (empty title); HTTP semantics (Location only valid with 3xx)

corrected_steps: Open a fresh browser context (Chromium, WebKit or Firefox, any width) and add cookies for localhost:3100: __convexAuthJWT=<any expired JWT> and __convexAuthRefreshToken=<any invalid or expired value>. Either cookie alone also triggers it.

Load http://localhost:3100/admin directly (also /admin/porudzbine, /nalog, /nalog/porudzbine, /majstor, /majstor/brza-porudzbina, /majstor/cenovnik) by typing the URL, from a bookmark or from an e-mail link.

Reload: you now reach /prijava, because the cookies were cleared on the first response.
Variant that does NOT break: load / first, let the session lapse, then click the header account link. Client-side navigation falls back to a full navigation and reaches /prijava.

corrected_steps: Open a fresh browser context and add cookies for localhost:3100: __convexAuthJWT=<any decodable JWT whose exp is in the past, e.g. header.{"sub":"x","iat":1700000000,"exp":1700003600}.sig> and __convexAuthRefreshToken=<unknown or revoked token>. Real-world equivalent: a session inactive for more than 14 days, or 30 days after sign-in, or signed out elsewhere.
Make the first request of the visit an account URL: /admin, /admin/porudzbine/SK-2026-000092 (a staff e-mail link), /nalog/porudzbine or /majstor.
Observe: HTTP 200, a Location header pointing to /prijava?next=..., a 0-byte body, a blank white page and an empty <title>.
Reload: you land on /prijava. Opening a public page first instead clears the cookies, and then the account URL returns a proper 307.

findings.title: Sign-in and registration forms send the password in the URL (GET) when submitted before hydration or without JavaScript
findings.context: 390 x 844, Chromium, JavaScript disabled (same native submit happens on a slow phone if the user presses Enter before the ~300 KB shell hydrates); consent cookie preset
steps: Open http://localhost:3100/prijava with JavaScript disabled (or throttle the network and submit before hydration).
Type an e-mail and a password and press Prijavi se.
Look at the address bar / the navigation request. Repeat on /registracija.
findings.expected: Credentials are never placed in a URL: the form either posts (method=post) to a handler that explains that JavaScript is needed, or the submit button stays inert until hydration.
findings.actual: The <form> has no method/action (SignInForm.tsx line 38: <form onSubmit noValidate>), so the browser performs GET /prijava?email=audit-a11y-app-nojs%40primer.rs&password=TajnaLozinka-555 (and GET /registracija?name=...&email=...&password=...). The plain-text password ends up in browser history, server/CDN access logs and any proxy logs.
findings.suggested_fix: components/auth/SignInForm.tsx and the registration form in components/auth/AuthForms.tsx: add method="post" (the POST to the page itself carries no credentials in the URL) and ideally an action to a small route handler/server action that answers 'Za prijavu je potreban JavaScript' without echoing input; alternatively render the submit button disabled until mounted. Check /za-majstore/registracija and /nalog/profil forms for the same pattern.

findings.title: Per-visitor rate limits include the caller-controlled User-Agent, so they are bypassable and the global order cap can be drained
findings.route: Every public write: /korpa checkout (orders:submit, carts cartCreate), /upit (inquiries:submit, inquiries:generateUploadUrl), back-in-stock subscribe, consent:record, search:log, /za-majstore (mechanics:register), quick order
findings.context: Dev deployment, anonymous ConvexHttpClient from one machine and IP with a custom fetch that sets the User-Agent header. Harmless mutation used (issuing an upload URL writes no business record).
steps: Run `node scripts/qa/audit/backend-ratelimit-ua.mjs`.
21 calls to inquiries:generateUploadUrl with one fixed User-Agent: 20 succeed and the 21st returns RATE_LIMITED (limit uploadUrl, 20/h per client).
21 more calls from the same IP, each with a different User-Agent: all 21 succeed, 0 limited.
findings.expected: Per-visitor limits hold for a given IP whatever headers the caller sends. No single public limit can be drained by one client to lock out every other customer.
findings.actual: The key is SHA-256(salt|ip|UA) (convex/lib/functions.ts:26-36, D4), and changing the UA gives a fresh bucket. The audit kit itself relies on this. Honeypot and the 3 s startedAt are client-supplied, so a script can submit unlimited inquiries and uploads (8 MB each) and create guest carts. It can also place orders until orderSubmitGlobal (fixed window, 300/h, convex/lib/rateLimits.ts:13) trips, after which every genuine customer gets „Previše pokušaja“ until the hour resets.
findings.suggested_fix: In getClientInfo (convex/lib/functions.ts), key per-client limits on the IP alone: salted hash, with the /64 prefix for IPv6. Keep the UA out of the key, or use ip+UA only as a second, finer bucket. Size the per-IP buckets for carrier NAT. Turn orderSubmitGlobal into a high alarm threshold that notifies the owner instead of a hard stop that blocks customers, or require sign-in/extra checks only above it. Add a convex-test proving two UAs from one IP share a bucket.
findings.standard: BRIEF §9 Security („rate limits on public writes“), SECURITY §L2, D4 (intent: real client IP limits)

verification.notes:
Reproduced independently with my own script, which uses a new UA prefix and a new ConvexHttpClient per call, against the harmless inquiries:generateUploadUrl (uploadUrl, 20/h per client key). (A) 21 calls with one fixed UA: 20 ok, the 21st RATE_LIMITED. (B) 10 calls, each with a new UA: 10 ok, 0 limited. (C) Control: the fixed UA from A again, 2 calls: both RATE_LIMITED. So the IP did not change between A and B, and B passed because of the UA alone. (D) Fixed UA plus a trailing space: still limited (header whitespace is normalised), so the UA really has to be different.

Skeptic checks:
- The key design is documented: D4, ARCHITECTURE §E6 and SECURITY.md D3 all say clientKey = SHA-256(salt + ip + UA). No reason for including the UA is written down.
- The bypass is not listed as an accepted risk in SECURITY-AUDIT §2.4 (R01–R11).
- The team knows about it and uses it only for tests: the te…
evidence: docs/qa/audit/verify/backend/backend-02-skeptic.json (A: 20 ok + RATE_LIMITED; B: 10/10 ok; C control: 2/2 RATE_LIMITED; D: 3/3 RATE_LIMITED)

convex/inquiries.ts:136 — only inquirySubmit per ctx.client.key; no per-e-mail or global inquiry limit
convex/events.ts:411-423 — inquiry.created sends inquiry_received to inquiry.contact.email (caller-supplied)
tests/e2e/storefront.spec.ts:21 — 'A unique user agent per run gives fresh per-client rate-limit buckets in Convex'
docs/DECISIONS.md D4 / docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §E6 — key design documented without a rationale for the UA; not in SECURITY-AUDIT §2.4 accepted risks
corrected_steps: Run `node scripts/qa/audit/verify-backend-02-skeptic.mjs` (anonymous ConvexHttpClient, custom User-Agent header, mutation inquiries:generateUploadUrl, no records written).
Phase A: 21 calls with one fixed UA. The first 20 return ok and the 21st returns RATE_LIMITED.
Phase B: 10 calls from the same machine and IP, each with a new UA. All 10 return ok.
Phase C (control): 2 more calls with the fixed UA from phase A. Both return RATE_LIMITED, which proves the IP did not change and the bypass comes from the UA alone.

Code path for impact: inquiries:submit is limited only by inquirySubmit on the same client key, and each accepted inquiry queues an inquiry_received e-mail to the submitted contact.email. So rotating the UA allows unlimited inquiries and confirmation e-mails to arbitrary addresses. The global order cap can only be drained with about 300 successful orders per hour, because failed submits roll back their global token.

findings.title: Product editor silently overwrites a price saved in another tab (or by an import) when an unrelated field is saved
findings.context: 1440x900 Chromium, owner, two tabs on the same product
steps: Sign in as owner and open the same product editor in tab A and tab B.
Tab A: change only Naziv. Do not save; the save bar shows 'Imate nesačuvane izmene.'
Tab B: change 'Maloprodajna cena sa PDV-om' from 4990 to 6.490,00 and press Ctrl+S. The server now holds 649000 para.
Tab A: the price field still shows 4990 and nothing says the product changed elsewhere. Press Ctrl+S.
Check the stored price with node node_modules/convex/bin/main.js run testing:productBySku '{"sku":"AUDIT-FA-852021"}', or look at /admin/revizija.
findings.expected: Tab A saves only the name, because only the name was changed there. If that isn't possible, the save is refused with a 'changed elsewhere' conflict (orders already do this with expectedUpdatedAt). Tab B's price 6.490 RSD stays.
findings.actual: The price goes back to 4.990 RSD (retailPricePara 499000) with no warning. The audit log records tab A's save as 'AUDIT-FA-852021: naziv, cena · Izmene (2)', so a price the user never touched was written. Cause: when the server document changes while the form is dirty, ProductEditor.tsx:301-310 replaces the baseline with the fresh server values but keeps the stale form values (it only refreshes stockQty). The diff at lines 332-342 then treats the stale price as a user edit. productsAdmin.update (convex/catalog/productsAdmin.ts:336) takes no expectedUpdatedAt. A bulk price change or an Excel import that lands while any editor has unsaved changes gets reverted the same way.
evidence: docs/qa/audit/flows-admin/v3-product.json (steps 'tab B saved' server 649000 → 'after tab A save' server 499000)
findings.suggested_fix: In ProductEditor.tsx, build the patch against the snapshot taken when editing started, per field (only fields where form !== original baseline). When the server changes while the form is dirty, rebase the untouched fields onto the fresh values and show a notice such as 'Artikal je u međuvremenu izmenjen — polja koja niste menjali su osvežena'. On the server, add expectedUpdatedAt to productsAdmin.update and throw CONFLICT on mismatch, as ordersAdmin already does, and handle it with the same 'Osvežite prikaz' message.
findings.standard: BRIEF §5/§6 (admin manages prices; the audit trail must reflect real changes) · BRIEF §9 Reliability · DESIGN-SYSTEM §10.12 (editor with sticky save bar)

steps: Open http://localhost:3100/ at 390×844 with touch emulation and consent pre-answered.

Add a tablet (768–1023 px) camera and poster instead of reusing the desktop right-offset composition, or centre the car when there is no copy column. Adjust the matching exploded cameras so the explode still fits. Regenerate the mobile/tablet posters (car-assembled-m-*, car-exploded-m-*, plus a tablet set) with npm run 3d so poster = canvas. findings.title: The mobile sticky buy bar never comes on screen: GSAP leaves it 71.5 px down, 7 px below the viewport, while it is marked visible and focusable
findings.context: Chromium 390×844 touch; normal motion (3 runs: 2× wheel, 1× scrollTo) and prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (1 run)
steps: Open http://localhost:3100/deo/kocioni-disk-prednji-276-24-mm-demo-0004 at 390×844.
Scroll past the inline „Dodaj u korpu“ button (its top is at 872 px), e.g. to scrollY 1300.
Wait 3 s and look at the bottom of the viewport; inspect div.fixed.bottom-0.z-sticky.
findings.expected: The sticky bottom buy bar (price, quantity, „Dodaj u korpu“) slides up (yPercent 110 → 0, 360 ms sk.out) and stays fully visible once the inline button has scrolled out, and slides away when it comes back (DS §10.3).
findings.actual: The bar is 65 px tall. The observer fires (visibility: visible, aria-hidden=false, inert removed), but the computed transform settles at translate(0, 71.5px), which puts its top at 851 px in an 844 px viewport, fully off-screen. This happened in 3/3 runs and was stable for 3 s. Under reduced motion the inline transform stays translateY(110%) and only the opacity animates, so the bar is again off-screen. Screenshots at the viewport bottom show no bar. Because the bar is no longer inert, keyboard users can Tab onto invisible quantity and add-to-cart controls.
findings.suggested_fix: In components/product/StickyBuyBar.tsx, remove the inline style transform "translateY(110%)" (line 55). GSAP parses it into y: 71.5px, and the show tween (line 38) only animates yPercent. Set the hidden state with gsap.set(el, { yPercent: 110, visibility: 'hidden' }) on mount inside useGSAP, and show with { y: 0, yPercent: 0 }. In the reduced branch, set yPercent: 0 immediately and fade the opacity. Keep SSR hidden via visibility only. Add an e2e: after scrolling past the inline button, the bar's boundingBox bottom ≤ viewport height.
findings.standard: DESIGN-SYSTEM §10.3 (mobile sticky bottom buy bar) and §8.5; BRIEF §9 Visual / conversion on the key mobile template; WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) for the focusable off-screen controls

verification.notes: Reproduced independently with my own script. At 390x844 Chromium, 3/3 normal-motion runs (2 wheel, 1 scrollTo 1300) ended with the bar at top 850.5 / bottom 915.5 in an 844 px viewport, so 0 px of it was visible. Computed transform was matrix(1,0,0,1,0,71.5), GSAP cache {y:'71.5px', yPercent:0}, visibility visible, aria-hidden=false, no inert, and it was the same 1 s later. The cause is in the code: GSAP 3.15 CSSPlugin _parseTransform (node_modules/gsap/CSSPlugin.js:1004) only recognises -50% as yPercent. The inline translateY(110%) from StickyBuyBar.tsx:55 is read as y=71.5px (110% of the 65 px bar), and the show tween at line 38 only animates yPercent to 0. With reduced motion the inline translateY(110%) is never touched (only opacity animates), so the bar again sits at top 850.5. The same happens in WebKit at 390 (top 850.5, transform 71.5155), in Chromium at 360x780 (top 786.5 > 780)…

findings.context: Lighthouse 13.5 mobile, --throttling devtools (slow 4G + 4× CPU), headless Chrome, fresh profile with the cookie banner visible, isolated server :3200. Shared machine: runs with benchmarkIndex < 3000 were excluded.

verification.notes: Lighthouse CLS on /vozila/volkswagen/golf/golf-7 is 0.082 in 3 of 3 mobile devtools runs and 0.074 in 2 of 2 desktop runs. The next/font fallback adjustment does not neutralise Martian Mono. The page misses BRIEF §9 CLS ≤ 0.05.

This is confirmed and the damage is wider than the finding says. I ran no Lighthouse and no timing runs. I only emulated the font swap on :3100 at scroll 0, using next/font's own fallback face.

**Cause.** ee9d8ff0751135e3 is the Martian Mono latin file (build CSS, preload:false). The fallback next/font generates is Arial at size-adjust 157.02 %. That size is calibrated on lowercase only. Advance width per em:
- Martian Mono: 0.700 for caps, digits and lowercase alike.
- The fallback: caps 1.064, digits 0.873, lowercase 0.713.

The codes are caps and digits (type-code-s also sets uppercase), so on first paint they are 25–52 % wider. In the chips, the code widths go 107–110 px → 81 px.

**Emulation matches Lighthouse.** At 412×823:
- mono alone: 0.0814 (Lighthouse devtools, section.mt-12: 0.08140)
- mono plus Archivo 600: 0.0994 (Lighthouse simulate: 0.1002)
- desktop 1350: 0.0711 (Lighth…

alsoReported.reason: Same header overflow, measured at the same 9 px at 360 px for signed-in mechanics. `iconLink` in components/shell/Header.tsx hard-codes `inline-flex`, so `hidden sm:inline-flex` never hides the icon links (AccountLink and the portal links). vis-commerce-02 finds the root cause and the go-live risk (the menu goes off-screen once phone and Viber are set). a11y-store-08's 3 px header overflow at 320 px is probably the same bug, but that finding stays open for the product-card clipping.

verification.notes:
Reproduced from scratch with my own script, which uses the exact Header.tsx class strings rather than a clone of the account link. Root cause checked in the built stylesheet .next/static/chunks/1ims1_lcdan5r.css: `.hidden{display:none}` sits at offset 17121 and `.inline-flex{display:inline-flex}` at 17200. Both have the same specificity, so the later inline-flex wins. As a result `iconLink + hidden sm:inline-flex` never hides anything, and the account link computes display:flex at 360 and 390. sm here is 30rem, i.e. 480 px.

Measured (Chromium isMobile):
- Guest today at 360 and 390: fits. At 360 the menu is at 300–344; the account icon shows but fits.
- Approved mechanic at 360 on /delovi: scrollWidth 369/360, menu 325–369, so the hamburger is cut by 9 px (visible in the screenshot). At 390 it just fits (menu 330–374).
- Guest with phone+Viber simulated: at 360, scrollWidth 415 and menu…

The header row is logo, search, Brza porudžbina, Majstorski portal, cart and menu. document.scrollWidth is 369 against a client width of 360, and 'Otvori meni' spans 325–369 px, so the hamburger is cut by 9 px.

In the same session, inspect the header account link [data-testid=account-button]. Its class holds both 'inline-flex' (from iconLink in components/shell/Header.tsx:23) and 'hidden sm:inline-flex'. getComputedStyle().display is 'flex', not 'none', at 360 and 390, although sm is 30rem (480 px). At 390x844 the menu sits at 371–415 and is cut by 25 px. With the phone alone, 360 already overflows by 9 px.
Control 1: hide the sm:inline-flex items below 480 px as the classes intend. At 360 the row is logo, search, phone, cart, menu, with the menu at 300–344, and nothing overflows.

Control 2: the ads landing /ponuda/kocione-plocice-golf uses its own header (app/(landing)/layout.tsx) with correct classes and is not affected. Affected scope: every SiteShell route (storefront (shop) group + not-found).

Expected per DESIGN-SYSTEM §10.1 (phone icon stays; Viber and account move to the menu on small screens): below sm the row is logo, search, phone, cart, menu, with nothing clipped at 360/390. Fix: remove display from the iconLink base class and apply `inline-flex` or `hidden sm:inline-flex` per link in components/shell/Header.tsx and components/shell/AccountLink.tsx (the quick-order and account links for mechanics included). Add an e2e check at 360 and 390 with a phone and Viber seeded that scrollWidth equals clientWidth and the menu trigger is fully in view.

findings.title: Chromium wipes text typed before hydration: the home hero search and the VIN inquiry (VIN + Opis) come back empty
findings.context: Chromium 153 headless, 390x844, isMobile. Tested two ways: (a) realistic Slow 4G (150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbps) with 4x CPU through CDP; (b) /_next/static/chunks delayed by 6 s. Guest, no vehicle selected. WebKit, same test: the text survives. Firefox: inconclusive, because the route delay did not hold back its chunks and the page hydrated before typing started. /prijava keeps its values in every engine.
steps: Open Chrome DevTools on http://localhost:3100/ at 390 px wide. Set Network to Slow 4G and CPU to 4x slowdown, then reload.
As soon as the hero field „Broj dela ili naziv“ appears (about 1.2–1.6 s), tap it and type 5Q0615505R.
Wait for hydration (about 3.3–3.8 s after navigation). The field is focused and empty again, showing only its placeholder.
Open http://localhost:3100/upit under the same throttling (or with JS chunks delayed). Before hydration, type VIN WVWZZZ1KZ8W123456 and, in Opis, „Turbina za Golf 7, dizel.“
After hydration both fields are empty. In a variant run the VIN stays visible, but its counter reads „0 / 17 znakova“ and the brand is not decoded.
Fill Ime and Telefon, tick the consent box and click „Pošalji upit“. The form blocks with „Napišite šta vam treba — naziv dela ili kvar.“
findings.expected: Text typed into a server-rendered field before React takes over stays in the field and reaches the form state. WebKit does this: the VIN is decoded to Volkswagen, the counter shows 25 / 2.000 and the inquiry submits (/upit/hvala/…).
findings.actual: In Chromium, React hydration clears what the visitor typed. Home hero search: erased in 3 of 3 realistic throttled runs (typing finished at 2.4–3.2 s, hydration at 3.3–3.8 s). /upit: VIN and Opis erased in 3 of 3 runs, and submit is refused with the required-field error. The DOM node is hydrated in place (same element), and only Chromium resets its value. This is the main mobile engine for Google/Meta ad traffic, and perf-lh-07 measures hydration about 3 s after first paint on slow phones, so a visitor typing an OEM number right away loses it.
evidence: docs/qa/audit/xbrowser/prehydration-real-chromium.json (3 runs: visibleAt 1212–1634 ms, typedAt 2355–3187 ms, hydratedAt 3325–3768 ms, after: "")

docs/qa/audit/xbrowser/prehydration-node-chromium_webkit.json (sameInput true in both engines; value "" in Chromium, VIN kept in WebKit)
docs/qa/audit/xbrowser/prehydration-forms-chromium_webkit.json (/prijava kept in both; home hero lost in Chromium only)
docs/qa/audit/xbrowser/inq-chromium-1440-error.webp (first sweep: VIN visible but „0 / 17 znakova“ and „0 / 2.000“)
findings.suggested_fix: components/shell/SearchBox.tsx: `const [query, setQuery] = useState(defaultQuery)` makes the hero input controlled, and hydration resets it. Seed the state from the server-rendered element in the initializer, e.g. `useState(() => (typeof document !== 'undefined' && (document.getElementById(inputId) as HTMLInputElement | null)?.value) || defaultQuery)`. components/inquiry/InquiryForm.tsx: `useForm({ defaultValues: { vin: '' … } })` with `register()` writes '' into the DOM when the ref attaches. Build defaultValues from the DOM (#iq-vin, the message textarea, name/phone/email/year) in a useState initializer before calling useForm. Alternatively render the form's fieldset disabled until mounted, with a visible loading state. Check CheckoutForm and the mechanic registration form the same way. Add an e2e test that delays /_next/static/chunks by 5 s, types, and asserts the value after hydration.
findings.standard: BRIEF §9 (world-class quality; core conversion flows for ad traffic on phones); DESIGN-SYSTEM §1 principle 5 „Workshop-proof … forgiving inputs“; BRIEF §3 users (mechanic on a phone, retail visitor from ads)

verification.notes: The wipe is real, but it is not Chromium-specific. The reviewer's WebKit 'survival' comes from their test setup. Their route pattern /_next/static/chunks/** also holds back the render-blocking CSS. In WebKit the field then appears together with the JS, so the page hydrates before or during typing: in my copy of their setup, hydratedAtVisible was true and hydration happened 18-28 ms after typing ended. When I held back only the .js chunks (CSS allowed through), WebKit behaved like Chromium. Home: '5Q0615505R' was in the DOM before hydration and was cleared about 390 ms after hydration. /upit: VIN and Opis were cleared in 2 of 2 runs, both counters showed 0, and submit was refused with 'Napišite šta vam treba — naziv dela ili kvar.' In one WebKit run hydration happened mid-typing and only 'R' was left, so a visitor can also end up with a truncated OEM number. Chromium: home wiped in 2/2 JS…
evidence: docs/qa/audit/verify/xbrowser/xbrowser-01-skeptic-webkit-delay-jsonly-home-390.json (run0: valueBeforeHydration '5Q0615505R', typedAt 3069, hydratedAt 8915, timeline -> '' at +391 ms; run1: hydration mid-typing, after 'R')
docs/qa/audit/verify/xbrowser/xbrowser-01-skeptic-webkit-delay-home-390.json (reviewer-style delay also holding CSS: hydratedAtVisible true / hydratedDuringTyping true, value kept - timing artefact)
docs/qa/audit/verify/xbrowser/xbrowser-01-skeptic-webkit-delay-jsonly-upit-390.json (2/2: VIN+Opis typed before hydration, after: vin '', msg '', counters 0 / 17 znakova, 0 / 2.000, submit blocked)
docs/qa/audit/verify/xbrowser/xbrowser-01-skeptic-chromium-cdp-home-390.json (Slow 4G + 4x CPU: run2 visible 2101 ms, typed 3754 ms, hydrated 4379 ms, wiped +429 ms)

corrected_steps: Use Chromium or WebKit at 390x844 (isMobile). Delay only the JavaScript: delay requests matching /_next/static/chunks/**/*.js by 6-8 s and let CSS through. Alternatively, in Chromium DevTools use Slow 4G with 4x CPU.
Open http://localhost:3100/. As soon as the hero field 'Broj dela ili naziv' is painted, tap it and type 5Q0615505R. Finish typing before hydration.

When React hydrates (the input gets __reactProps), the field empties within about 100-450 ms and keeps focus. If hydration lands mid-typing, only the characters typed after it may remain (for example 'R').
Open http://localhost:3100/upit under the same conditions. Before hydration, type the VIN WVWZZZ1KZ8W123456 and, in Opis, 'Turbina za Golf 7, dizel.'

After hydration both fields are empty, and the counters read '0 / 17 znakova' and '0 / 2.000'. Fill Ime and Telefon, tick the consent box and click 'Pošalji upit'. The form blocks with 'Napišite šta vam treba — naziv dela ili kvar.'
The same result occurs in WebKit and Chromium. The defect is engine-independent (React 19.2.8 does not replay input made before hydration).

verification.notes: The defect is real, but it is not specific to Chromium. It reproduces in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox whenever typing ends before hydration, and it affects more forms than reported. My first run copied the reporter's method, delaying everything under /_next/static/chunks/**. That also delays the render-blocking CSS, so the form only became visible at about 6.5 s, the same moment JS arrived. In WebKit, typing then overlapped hydration (hydratedAt 7625 ms, typedAt 7617 ms), the text survived and the inquiry submitted. That is where the reporter's 'WebKit keeps it' result comes from. With only .js chunks delayed, the form is visible at 0.2–1.1 s and typing finishes at 0.9–2.7 s. Hydration then comes at about 6.3–6.8 s, and all three engines lose the text on the same node (sameNode true). Home hero after hydration: value "" in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox. /upit after hydration: vin "", msg …
evidence: docs/qa/audit/verify/xbrowser/xbrowser-01-reproduce-chromium_webkit_firefox-390-home_upit.json (JS-only 6 s delay: home after.value "" and /upit vin/msg "" plus submit error in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox)

docs/qa/audit/verify/xbrowser/xbrowser-01-reproduce-chromium_webkit-390-home_upit.json (first run delaying CSS too: page visible at about 6.5 s, WebKit typing overlaps hydration, text kept and submit reaches /upit/hvala/…; this is the artefact behind the 'WebKit survives' claim)
docs/qa/audit/verify/xbrowser/xbrowser-01-reproduce-real-chromium-390-home-after.webp (hero shows truncated „5505R“ and „Prikaži sve rezultate za „5505R““)
docs/qa/audit/verify/xbrowser/xbrowser-01-reproduce-real-scope.json (/prijava and /registracija keep text; /za-majstore/registracija goes to ""; /pretraga goes back to „disk“)
docs/qa/audit/verify/xbrowser/xbrowser-01-reproduce-prijava.json (uncontrolled SignInForm: values reach submit, server says „Pogrešan e-mail ili lozinka“)
corrected_steps: Any engine (Chromium, WebKit or Firefox), any width (checked at 390 and 1440). Hold back only the JS chunks: in Playwright, route **/_next/static/chunks/**/*.js with a 6 s delay and let CSS through. Or in Chrome DevTools, set Slow 4G + 4x CPU with the cache disabled.
Open http://localhost:3100/. As soon as the hero field „Broj dela ili naziv“ is painted, tap it and type 5Q0615505R, finishing before hydration.

Wait for hydration (the input gets __reactProps). The field empties to its placeholder. If hydration lands mid-typing, the field keeps only the last characters (e.g. „5505R“) and suggests „Prikaži sve rezultate za „5505R““.
Open /upit the same way. Before hydration, type VIN WVWZZZ1KZ8W123456 and, in Opis, „Turbina za Golf 7, dizel.“. After hydration both are empty and the counters read 0 / 17 and 0 / 2.000.
Fill Ime and Telefon, tick consent and click „Pošalji upit“. The form refuses with „Napišite šta vam treba — naziv dela ili kvar.“
The same loss happens on /za-majstore/registracija (e-mail field goes to "") and in the /pretraga?q=disk search box (goes back to „disk“). /prijava is not affected (uncontrolled inputs + FormData).

Suggested fix: use the uncontrolled + FormData pattern of components/auth/SignInForm.tsx where possible. Otherwise, in components/shell/SearchBox.tsx, sync state from the DOM in a mount useLayoutEffect (if inputRef.value differs from state, setQuery(inputRef.value)). In components/inquiry/InquiryForm.tsx and components/mechanic/MechanicRegistrationForm.tsx, read the server-rendered field values in a useState initializer (runs during the hydration render, before register() refs write '') and pass them as defaultValues. Add an e2e test that delays only JS chunks, types, and asserts the value and a successful submit after hydration, in Chromium and WebKit.

findings.title: Cookie banner fully covers the focused element on first visit (21 tab stops at 390, 7 at 1440), and Escape does not dismiss it
findings.route: Every storefront route on a first visit (no sk_consent cookie), e.g. /delovi/kocioni-diskovi
findings.context: 390x844 and 1440x900 Chromium, consent:false, keyboard only
steps: Open /delovi/kocioni-diskovi in a fresh context without the sk_consent cookie
Without answering the banner, press Tab through the page (skip link, then banner, then header, then product cards)
Check the focused element's rectangle against the banner rectangle
Press Escape
findings.expected: A focused element is never entirely hidden by author-created content. The page scrolls it above the banner (scroll-padding-bottom), or the banner can be collapsed or dismissed.
findings.actual: At 390 the banner is 314 px tall (37 % of the viewport, top at 530 px). 21 consecutive tab stops (card links and „U korpu“ buttons) are 100 % covered, and the orange focus ring sits under the banner. At 1440, 7 stops are covered. Escape leaves the banner open. Reproduced in 2 runs.
findings.suggested_fix: In components/consent/ConsentBanner.tsx, while the banner is mounted, set document.documentElement.style.scrollPaddingBottom to the banner height plus 16 px (ResizeObserver) and clear it on unmount, so focused elements scroll above it. Also shorten the mobile layout: put the two decision buttons side by side and turn „Podešavanja“ into a link-style button to cut the height. Optionally let Escape collapse it to a one-line bar. D185 (non-modal banner) stays valid. This finding is about obscuring focus, not modality.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum); DESIGN-SYSTEM §12.1 rule 2 (focus not obscured by sheets)

verification.notes: I reproduced this from scratch with my own script: consent:false, Tab x50 from page load, and each focused rect compared with the visible banner panel (the <form>, not the transparent full-width wrapper). Checked in Chromium and Firefox. /delovi/kocioni-diskovi at 390: the panel is 366x302 at y=530 (36 % of the viewport). 22 of 50 stops are 100 % hidden (card titles, 'U korpu'/'Poruči', vehicle landing links, footer logo) and 2 are partly hidden. The reviewer's '21 consecutive' is wrong. The hidden stops are interleaved: the longest run is 7, then the browser scrolls once the next stop leaves the viewport and the next three are hidden again. At 1440 the reviewer's '7 stops' is overstated because it was measured against the transparent inset-x-0 wrapper. The visible panel is x=144..1296, so the filter checkboxes at x=48 stay visible. findings.title: Pressing „Podešavanja“ in the cookie banner drops focus to <body>
findings.route: Every storefront route on a first visit, e.g. /delovi/kocioni-diskovi
findings.context: 390x844 and 1440x900 Chromium, consent:false, keyboard
steps: Open a page without the sk_consent cookie
Tab to the banner's „Podešavanja“ and press Enter
Check document.activeElement
findings.expected: Focus moves into the newly shown settings (the first enabled switch „Analitika“ or the „Kategorije kolačića“ group) so keyboard and screen-reader users know the content changed.
findings.actual: The focused button is unmounted (setDetailed(true)) and focus falls to BODY at both widths. The screen-reader user gets no announcement and must Tab from the top of the document (the banner is 2nd in the order, so the switches are reachable, but the context is lost).

findings.suggested_fix: In ConsentBanner.tsx, add a useEffect on `detailed` that focuses the first enabled switch (or a tabIndex=-1 legend of „Kategorije kolačića“) when it becomes true.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order; DESIGN-SYSTEM §12.1 rule 5

findings.title: Consent and terms checkbox errors are not programmatically linked to the checkbox (checkout, inquiry, mechanic registration)
findings.context: 1440x900 Chromium, guest, keyboard
steps: Complete checkout steps 1–3 (pickup, cash) and on „Pregled“ press Enter on „Pošalji porudžbinu“ without ticking the terms
Focus the checkbox #co-terms and read its accessible description
Repeat on /upit: submit empty and inspect the consent checkbox
findings.expected: The checkbox has aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby pointing at the visible error text, like every text field in these forms.
findings.actual:
#co-terms has aria-invalid="true" but an empty description (desc: ""). The error

has no id and is not referenced. The same pattern exists in InquiryForm (consent) and MechanicRegistrationForm (terms). Focusing the checkbox announces „invalid“ with no reason.
findings.suggested_fix:
Give each error

an id (e.g. co-terms-error) and pass it to Checkbox as aria-describedby, merged with its own descriptionId in components/ui/Checkbox.tsx. Better: let Checkbox accept an `error` prop and render and link the message itself, as Field does.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, SC 3.3.1 Error Identification; DESIGN-SYSTEM §12.1 rule 7 („inline errors linked with aria-describedby“)

alsoReported.title: Consent checkbox errors are not programmatically tied to the checkbox (no aria-invalid, no aria-describedby)

findings.title: Order line edits never adjust stock that was already committed, so stock drifts in the „pri kreiranju“ decrement mode

findings.title: The global sign-up limit can be drained by anyone and closes registration for all customers and mechanics
findings.context: Code review plus the deployed function spec. Not executed: draining the bucket would lock out other reviewers.
steps: `auth:signIn` is a public action on the deployment (deployed-function-spec-summary.txt), callable directly on https://<deployment>.convex.cloud without going through the Next /api/auth proxy.

A script calls it 30 times with flow "signUp", random e-mails and a valid password. Each new account consumes the single "global" key of signUpGlobal (token bucket capacity 30, 60/h; convex/auth.ts:90, convex/lib/rateLimits.ts:25).

Every genuine visitor registering on /registracija, including mechanics who must create an account before the /za-majstore registration, then gets RATE_LIMITED. About one sign-up a minute from the script keeps registration closed indefinitely.
findings.expected: Abuse by one client cannot block registration for everyone. D207 accepts a global limit because the IP is hidden behind the Next proxy, but the action is also directly reachable, and the result breaks the BRIEF §5 mechanics onboarding flow.
findings.actual: The only sign-up control is one shared global bucket.
findings.suggested_fix: Enable e-mail verification (R01/D212) so junk sign-ups do not become active accounts. Key sign-up limits on the caller IP where Convex request metadata is available, or on a signed client-IP header forwarded by the /api/auth proxy with direct calls refused. Keep the global number as an owner alert rather than a hard stop.
findings.standard: BRIEF §5 Mechanics (registration flow), BRIEF §9 Security; D207 documented, but the trade-off breaks the BRIEF as shown

verification.notes: I did not drain the shared bucket. I reproduced each part without spending a sign-up token. (1) I called the public auth:signIn action directly on <deployment>.eu-west-1.convex.cloud through ConvexHttpClient, skipping the Next proxy, with flow signUp and a 5-character password. The backend ran the sign-up flow and answered ConvexError WEAK_PASSWORD. The Password provider validates the password before it creates an account, so no user was created and no token was spent. This shows the sign-up path is directly reachable. (2) A read-only lookup (rateLimiter lib:getValue) shows a single shared bucket, signUpGlobal/'global': token bucket, capacity 30, 60 per hour (1 per minute), value 28.1 at the time. convex/auth.ts:90 spends one token per new user. The proxy (proxy.ts, convexAuthNextjsMiddleware) has no per-client limit either, so a single client can empty the bucket through /api/auth as we…
evidence: docs/qa/audit/verify/backend/backend-07-reproduce.json (direct convex.cloud auth:signIn signUp -> WEAK_PASSWORD; signUpGlobal/global bucket capacity 30, rate 60/h, value 28.11)
docs/qa/audit/verify/backend/backend-07-proxy-error.txt (proxy returns HTTP 400 {"error":"[Request ID…] Server Error Uncaught ConvexError: {…}"}, so the ConvexError data is lost)
docs/qa/audit/verify/backend/backend-07-reproduce-signup-390.webp and -1440.webp (sign-up with a simulated RATE_LIMITED response shows the 'Ako već imate nalog…' fallback)
corrected_steps: Run node scripts/qa/audit/verify-backend-07-signup.mjs. It calls auth:signIn directly on the Convex URL with flow signUp and a weak password, gets WEAK_PASSWORD (the sign-up flow is reachable without the proxy), and reads the single signUpGlobal/'global' bucket (capacity 30, 60/h).

Code path: every new user runs afterUserCreatedOrUpdated, which calls enforceRateLimit(signUpGlobal, 'global') (convex/auth.ts:90). A script making 30 sign-ups, then 1 per minute, keeps the bucket at 0, whether it calls Convex directly or goes through /api/auth (the proxy has no per-client limit).

Run node scripts/qa/audit/verify-backend-07-ui.mjs. It fulfils the sign-up POST /api/auth with the exact 400 body the proxy produces for RATE_LIMITED. /registracija then shows 'Nalog nije napravljen. Ako već imate nalog sa ovom adresom, prijavite se ili promenite lozinku.' instead of a 'try again later' message. /za-majstore/registracija shows 'Nalog sa ovom e-mail adresom verovatno već postoji'.

Suggested fix: enable e-mail verification (R01/D212). Key the sign-up limit on the request IP from ctx.meta.getRequestMetadata() for direct calls, and on a proxy-signed client key for /api/auth, and keep the global number as an owner alert. Map proxy error strings containing RATE_LIMITED to the Serbian 'Previše pokušaja…' message in AuthForms and MechanicRegistrationForm (parse the code out of error.message, since the Next client drops .data).

findings.title: Quick order: an existing code with quantity 0 or above 999 is reported as „nije pronađeno“ and forwarded to staff as an unknown part
findings.context: Chromium 1440x900, audit mechanic
steps: Open /majstor/brza-porudzbina as the mechanic.
Paste `5Q0615505R 0` and `5Q0615505R 1000` (DEMO-0004, in stock) and `ZZ9999999`. Click „Proveri brojeve“.
Rows 3 and 4 show „NIJE PRONAĐENO — Ovaj broj nemamo u katalogu. Pošaljite ga u upitu“.
Click „Pošalji upit za nepronađene (3)“, then open the inquiry in admin.
findings.expected: The code is matched and the row shows a quantity error („Količina 0 nije ispravna — upišite 1–999“ or „Najviše 999 kom. po redu“). No inquiry is suggested for a part that is in stock.
findings.actual: `toQuantity()` rejects 0 and anything above 999, and a 4-digit tail fails `/^\d{1,3}$/`, so the quantity is glued onto the code (normalised `5Q0615505R0`, `5Q0615505R1000`) and the line is reported as not in the catalogue. The one-click inquiry UP-2026-000079 reached staff with „Traženi brojevi: 5Q0615505R0, 5Q0615505R1000, ZZ9999999“, so staff get a quote request for a part the shop has on the shelf.
findings.suggested_fix: lib/domain/quickOrder.ts: when the last token is all digits (up to 5), also emit a candidate where that token is the quantity, carrying a `quantityError` („0“ / „> 999“) instead of discarding it. The server match then finds the code, and QuickOrder.tsx shows the row as TAČNO with an inline quantity error and a stepper clamped to 1–999. Keep unknown-code inquiries for real misses only.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1 Error Identification / 3.3.3 Error Suggestion; BRIEF §9 mechanics quick order (not found → inquiry only when truly missing)

verification.notes: Chromium 1440x900, audit mechanic. Checked `5Q0615505R 0`, `5Q0615505R 1000`, `ZZ9999999`, `5q0-615-505-r 0` and `5Q0615505R 1500`. The CSV form `5Q0615505R;1000` matches TAČNO but silently drops the quantity to 1, with no notice. Only `5Q0615505R 999` works: it matches and shows the „Na stanju je još 2 kom.“ warning. The inquiry button then offers „Pošalji upit za nepronađene (7)“, 6 of them for an in-stock part. The line then falls through to candidate(text,1), so the digits are glued onto the code (5Q0615505R0 / 5Q0615505R1000). inquireMissing normalises and stores these as r…

findings.title: The site-wide text reveal costs about 230–400 ms of rAF work plus 300 ms of start-up per load at 4× CPU: per-word GSAP tweens animate filter blur with will-change on every word
findings.context: Playwright Chromium, 412 × 823, 4× CPU via CDP, devtools.timeline trace from navigation to load + 5 s; consent pre-answered
steps: Run: AUDIT_BASE=http://localhost:3200 PATHS=/delovi/kocioni-diskovi,/deo/kocioni-disk-prednji-276-24-mm-demo-0004,/kontakt node scripts/qa/audit/perf-lh-trace.mjs 1
Read docs/qa/audit/perf-lh/trace-attribution.json: rafCount/rafMs, perScript['1tr6a7zmh41cy.js'] and the longTasks with FireAnimationFrame.
Compare with components/TextRevealGlobal.tsx lines 124–147: gsap.set on every word span with opacity, filter blur(8px), y, willChange 'transform, opacity, filter', then a staggered tween.
findings.expected: Copy entrance animations stay on the compositor (transform/opacity), stay out of the TBT window and add no long tasks (gsap-performance: avoid many simultaneous tweens of paint-heavy properties).
findings.actual:
Category: 333 rAF callbacks totalling 397 ms and GSAP function calls of 293 ms in the first 5 s. Long tasks of 74–249 ms are dominated by FireAnimationFrame plus UpdateLayoutTree (30–66 ms) and Commit (33 ms). The app chunk that holds TextRevealGlobal (25dplrt_qw3he.js) also runs a 298 ms task at hydration, with 68 ms of style and 74 ms of layout inside: the :has()-based hiddenSelector query and its observers.
Product: 456 rAF, 227 ms. /kontakt: 454 rAF, 234 ms.
Lighthouse bootup-time attributes 1.2–2.45 s to the GSAP chunk at 4×. The attempted A/B (reveal CSS/JS stripped) was too noisy on the shared machine to quantify the saving; see not_covered.
findings.suggested_fix:
1. Drive the word animation with a CSS keyframe that is already inlined for RevealText (the tr-lcp pattern with --i/--n). TextRevealGlobal would then only split the words, set --i and toggle a class, with no per-frame GSAP work.
2. Drop filter: blur on coarse pointers or at small widths, or animate opacity and transform only.
3. Start the IntersectionObserver in requestIdleCallback after hydration.
4. Precompute eligibility on the server (e.g. a data attribute from RevealText-like helpers) so the runtime query does not evaluate the nested :has() selector across the document.
findings.standard: BRIEF §9 (TBT ≤ 200 ms); gsap-performance (prefer transform/opacity, avoid mass filter tweens, will-change only while animating); .claude/rules/architecture.md Text Reveal (the no-second-animation rule still holds)

findings.title: On slow phones the text-reveal failsafe fires before hydration: copy stays hidden about 3 s after first paint, then already-visible lines are hidden again and re-animated
findings.context: Playwright Chromium 412 × 823, 4× CPU + Lighthouse slow-4G (562.5 ms RTT, 1.47 Mbps) via CDP, consent pre-answered
steps: Run: AUDIT_BASE=http://localhost:3200 node scripts/qa/audit/perf-lh-failsafe.mjs 2

Read docs/qa/audit/perf-lh/failsafe.json: fcp, failsafeAt (html.tr-failsafe added), firstStateAt (TextRevealGlobal's first data-reveal-state) and splitAfterFailsafe (elements set to 'running' after the failsafe).
Read components/TextRevealGlobal.tsx lines 73–76: it clears the timer but never checks html.tr-failsafe.
findings.expected: Copy is readable soon after first paint on a mid-range phone. If the failsafe has revealed copy, the observer must not hide it again (.claude/rules/architecture.md: the failsafe reveals everything if the observer never starts).
findings.actual:
- FCP: 2.05–3.3 s.
- tr-failsafe: 5.30–5.77 s (3.5 s after the head boot script).
- TextRevealGlobal starts only at 5.86–7.84 s.
So every non-RevealText line in the first viewport is opacity 0 for about 3 s after first paint. After the failsafe has shown it, 6 elements on category and 2 on product and landing are split and animated from opacity 0 again: a visible flash and extra main-thread work after load. LCP is not affected; the LCP elements are RevealText or data-reveal="off".
findings.suggested_fix:
1. In TextRevealGlobal, if html has tr-failsafe, mark every candidate done and do not re-hide (in reveal(), check the class before gsap.set).
2. Either arm the failsafe relative to the `load`/hydration time, or hide at boot only candidates below the first viewport, so above-the-fold copy never waits for hydration.
3. Make hydration cheaper (perf-lh-01), which also shortens the hidden window.
findings.standard: DESIGN-SYSTEM §8.6 / .claude/rules/architecture.md (Text Reveal behaviour, failsafe); ARCHITECTURE risk R5 ('text reveal hides content'); BRIEF §9 visual quality

verification.notes: At 412 px, 4× CPU and slow 4G, 2 rounds on each of 4 paths: FCP 1996–2148 ms, tr-failsafe at 5237–5317 ms, TextRevealGlobal's first state at 5568–5666 ms. After the failsafe, 6 elements are split again on category and 2 on product and landing (home 0). Snapshot at 3.99 s, 1.9 s after FCP: 8 copy elements in the first viewport are at opacity 0, so the product cards show image, stock, price and 'U korpu' but no product name, brand or OEM number. At 5.78 s, after the failsafe had shown them, the titles and OEM lines are blurred word spans at opacity 0 again, being re-animated. Code: TextRevealGlobal.tsx:75 only clears the timer and reveal() never checks tr-failsafe. Raised to P1: this is a first-impression defect on the category ad-landing template under the standard lab mobile profile. The hidden window follows the documented 3.5 s failsafe timing, but the re-hide contradicts the text-reve…

The re-hide is a real logic bug, and its scope is wider than reported. TextRevealGlobal.tsx:75 only calls clearTimeout, and neither track() nor reveal() checks html.tr-failsafe. Once the failsafe has fired, the CSS gate stays off for the rest of the session, yet every candidate is still tracked and split from opacity 0.

Deterministic check (no throttling; the boot script's 3500 ms timer forced to 0 ms; category page at 412 px):
- First load: 6 of 6 above-the-fold elements were painted at opacity 1 and then split to 0.
- Scrolling: 22 of 22 lines were visible in the bottom 15% band, then went blank and re-animated as they crossed the observer line.
- Client navigation to a product: the new copy was not hidden by CSS (opacity 1 while pending) and was then split.
- Control run with the real timer: 0 in every case.

Where I disagree:
(1) The ~3.3 s hidden window after FCP (2.0 s to 5.3 s) i…

lib/textRevealCss.ts: hiding rule is html.tr-js:not(.tr-failsafe) …, so after the failsafe nothing is CSS-hidden for the session
.lighthouse/_delovi_kocioni-diskovi-mobile-devtools-4.json and -5.json (uncontended: CSS ends ~1.6 s, last first-load JS ends ~3.95 s)
corrected_steps: Run node scripts/qa/audit/verify-perf-lh-07-perfskeptic.mjs against :3100. It opens /delovi/kocioni-diskovi in Chromium at 412×823 with consent set, and an init script wraps window.setTimeout so the boot script's 3500 ms failsafe fires at 0 ms. This reproduces 'hydration finished after the failsafe' on any machine.

First load: 6 first-viewport elements ("Više o kategoriji", the brand lines, the h3 product names, the OEM lines) have data-reveal-state=pending with computed opacity 1, then become running with word spans at opacity 0. The copy is visible, then goes blank, then re-animates.
Scroll to the end: all 22 remaining lines are visible as they enter the bottom 15% of the viewport, then blank out and re-animate as they cross the IntersectionObserver line.

Real-world trigger: hydration has to finish more than 3.5 s after the stylesheet loads (the boot script runs after it). Under the D112 lab profile (4× CPU, slow 4G) this is borderline (lost by 0 to ~400 ms in prior runs). It happens reliably on slower-than-lab devices.

findings.title: The Lighthouse gate tests/lighthouse/run.mjs does not enforce the BRIEF budgets, and four bugs lose data
findings.context: Runner used as documented in WEB-QA §2 and TESTING §M
steps: Read tests/lighthouse/run.mjs line 34: `const BUDGET = { lcp: 2500, cls: 0.05, tbt: 300, performance: 0.85 }`.

Run: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 node tests/lighthouse/run.mjs --base http://localhost:3200 --runs 3 --desktop / /delovi/kocioni-diskovi. `/` is silently skipped; see lh-console.log line 105 onward, where only category and product ran.
Run any batch with --runs 5 --throttling devtools / on a loaded machine. When one run returns NO_NAVSTART, the script crashes at `run.cls.toFixed` and every remaining URL is lost.
Observe `LCP element:` printed empty on every run.
findings.expected: The gate encodes BRIEF §9 and step 22: TBT ≤ 200 ms, perf ≥ 90 for catalog/product, a11y ≥ 95, SEO ≥ 95 on indexable pages, SEO-ADS JS bytes. It survives a failed run and reports the LCP element.
findings.actual:
1. TBT budget is 300 ms (BRIEF 200); performance is a flat 85 (BRIEF: 90 for catalog/product); there are no a11y, SEO, best-practices or JS-byte gates. /delovi at 91/246 ms printed 'budgets met'.
2. Three runs in this audit hit NO_NAVSTART; each crash aborted the rest of its batch.
3. The LCP element is always empty, because Lighthouse 13 removed `largest-contentful-paint-element`; the data is now in lcp-breakdown-insight.
4. A path that directly follows the boolean --desktop is parsed as the flag's value and dropped: `/` and `/delovi` were never run on desktop.
evidence: docs/qa/audit/perf-lh/lh-console.log (lines 2–10, 19–27, 96–104 crashes; 17, 34, 46 empty LCP element; 53 'budgets met' at TBT 246; 105–106 '/' skipped)
scripts/qa/audit/perf-lh-fill.mjs (workaround: one run per call + retry)
findings.suggested_fix:
In tests/lighthouse/run.mjs:
- Set per-template budgets from BRIEF §9 / SEO-ADS §J11 (tbt 200; perf 0.90 for /delovi*, /deo/*, /ponuda/*; a11y and SEO ≥ 0.95 unless the page is noindex; a JS-bytes gate).
- Skip and retry runs with lhr.runtimeError instead of dereferencing missing metrics.
- Read the LCP node from audits['lcp-breakdown-insight'].details.items (type 'node').
- Treat only known value flags (--base, --runs, --throttling) as consuming the next argument.
- Record environment.benchmarkIndex and reject runs below a threshold.
findings.standard: BRIEF §9; docs/TESTING.md §M; Definition of Done (reliable quality gates)

verification.notes:
Static checks, all reproduced:
- tests/lighthouse/run.mjs:35 sets tbt 300 and a flat performance 0.85, with no a11y, SEO or JS-bytes gates, although TESTING.md says the runner checks §J11.
- The path filter on line 29 drops a path that follows --desktop: simulating the args '--desktop / /delovi/kocioni-diskovi' gives only ['/delovi/kocioni-diskovi'].
- Lighthouse 13.5.0 has no largest-contentful-paint-element audit, so the LCP element is always empty.
- `run.cls.toFixed` is called on undefined when a run fails; the finder's log shows the TypeError at line 7.
I saw no NO_NAVSTART in my 30 runs; my own runner skips failed runs.

findings.title: 3D start freezes the main thread for 0.3–0.9 s at the visitor's first touch, scroll or hover (the PMREM shader compiles synchronously, the first frame still links programs, the 3D chunk evaluates)
findings.context: Chromium 1.63 headless, ANGLE D3D11 (RTX 4060 Laptop). Desktop 1440×900 at DPR 1, CPU 1× and 4×. Mobile 390×844 at DPR 3 with touch, CPU 4× and 6×. Anonymous visitor, consent answered, first visit (fresh browser, so the GPU program cache is cold). Server: localhost:3200.
steps: Launch a fresh Chromium with --use-angle=d3d11 --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist and open http://localhost:3200/. Wait for load.
Optional: set the CPU throttle with CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate {rate: 4}.
Give intent: on desktop move the pointer over the hero stage; on mobile tap the stage or scroll more than 40 px.

Record a CPU profile and the long tasks until window.__sklop3d.getState().status === 'ready'. Scripted: `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-profile.mjs --vp desktop --cpu 1 --gpu`, run 3 times (each run launches a new browser); `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-frames.mjs --vp mobile --cpu 4 --gpu --runs 3`; and `... --cold` to make the first scroll the intent.
findings.expected: The 3D never blocks the page. The init runs in short tasks (WEB-QA §4 records tasks ≤ 175 ms), and compileAsync plus idle slices keep scrolling and taps responsive while the model comes up (BRIEF §4, contract F7.3).
findings.actual: PMREMGenerator.fromEquirectangular → _applyGGXFilter → getUniforms → getProgramParameter blocks while the PMREM blur shader compiles: 336, 344 and 457 ms at 1× CPU on three fresh browsers (busy stretches 378–519 ms), and 725–884 ms at 4×. The 3D chunk (282 KB gzip) takes 255–345 ms to evaluate at 4×. The first real frame after compileAsync still blocks 160–190 ms in getProgramParameter plus 52–92 ms of texSubImage2D, although KHR_parallel_shader_compile is available. Worst start long task: desktop 4× 556/291/434 ms (start TBT 604–1113 ms); mobile 4× 765/294/313 ms (TBT 527–1603 ms); mobile 6× 897/435/616 ms (TBT 1267–2293 ms). When the first scroll on a phone is the intent (4×), a single frame in the middle of the scroll takes 683, 333 and 300 ms (3/3 runs). A warm program cache cuts the PMREM cost to about 77 ms, but first-time visitors (ad traffic) always pay the full cost.
findings.suggested_fix: components/three/canvas/loadCar.ts loadEnvironment(): stop prefiltering at runtime. Bake the PMREM output (cubeUV layout) in the 3D pipeline, export it as a half-float/RGBE PNG or KTX2, load it with mapping = CubeUVReflectionMapping and drop PMREMGenerator and HDRLoader. If that is not possible, compile the PMREM blur material through KHR_parallel_shader_compile first (compileAsync on a throwaway mesh) before calling fromEquirectangular. In HeroCanvas.tsx, include every material the first frame uses (edge and depth materials, overlay layer) in the compileAsync pass, and initTexture every texture before compileAsync. On fine-pointer devices, import and evaluate the canvas chunk in idle time before intent. Then correct the numbers in docs/3d/WEB-QA.md §4.
findings.standard: BRIEF §4 (the 3D must never block the page); 3D-CONTRACT F7.3 (compileAsync, idle slices); DESIGN-SYSTEM §1 principle 5 (3D never blocks); docs/3d/WEB-QA.md §4 (init in tasks ≤ 175 ms); INP ≤ 200 ms

verification.notes: CPU profile on a fresh browser at 1×: PMREM fromEquirectangular → getProgramParameter is a busy stretch of 390 ms (350 ms self), and the first frame after compileAsync 242 ms (148 ms getProgramParameter). A warm program cache in the same browser cuts this to 15 ms and 76 ms. At 4×, cold: PMREM 558 ms, first frame and compileAsync 357 ms, canvas chunk evaluation 178 ms. Frames runs, worst start long task: mobile 4× 520/389/230 ms (sum over 50 ms 936/652/381), desktop 4× 472/199/228 ms (818/324/425). This contradicts WEB-QA §4's 'tasks ≤ 175 ms'. Lowered to P2: the freeze follows an explicit intent, happens once per cold visit and blocks no flow; BRIEF's 'never block the page' is about loading after first paint, which holds. The --cold first-scroll case was not re-run.

Analysis only: I ran no browser. I re-read the finder's and the perf verifier's JSON and profiles with an offline script, then checked the code. CONFIRMED: on a first visit (cold GPU program cache), Windows ANGLE D3D11 compiles the PMREM GGX shader synchronously. loadCar.ts:96-105 calls pmrem.fromEquirectangular(), which uses the three 0.186.1 GGX filter with a 256-sample loop. Nothing precompiles it; compileAsync in HeroCanvas.tsx:126 covers only the scene materials. At 1x CPU this is a single getProgramParameter wait of 336/344/457 ms (finder, 3 launches) and 350 ms (verifier). The first frame after compileAsync adds 138-191 ms. With a warm cache in the same browser, desktop 1x start TBT drops from 525 ms (run 0) to 8/0 ms (runs 1-2). The shader compile alone is enough to explain the 1x cost. The compile time does not depend on the network, so this is not a localhost artefact. NARROWER…
corrected_steps: Use Windows with Chrome or Edge on ANGLE D3D11 (Playwright: chromium.launch({args:['--use-angle=d3d11','--enable-gpu','--ignore-gpu-blocklist']})). Use a NEW browser launch for every measured run: a new context in the same browser reuses the in-memory GPU program cache, and the problem disappears.
Open http://localhost:3200/ at 1440x900, DPR 1, CPU 1x, with consent answered. Wait for load.
Move the pointer over the hero stage (intent). Record a CPU profile until window.__sklop3d.getState().status === 'ready'.

Expected: no task over 50-100 ms. Actual (cold): one task of about 340-460 ms. Its self time is getProgramParameter under PMREMGenerator.fromEquirectangular → _applyGGXFilter. A second task of about 200-250 ms follows (138-191 ms getProgramParameter in the first render after compileAsync). Start TBT is about 525 ms.
Control: repeat in the same browser (warm cache). Start TBT is 0-8 ms at 1x, and PMREM takes about 15 ms.

Do not count the canvas chunk evaluation (turbopack H, about 20 ms at 1x, 255-489 ms at 4x/6x) toward this finding. It is the budgeted lazy chunk. Phone numbers need a real phone GPU backend, not a desktop D3D11 run with CPU throttling.

findings.title: Every home visit leaks the old WebGL renderer, its canvas and the whole detached home DOM (+1107 DOM nodes per visit)
findings.context: Desktop 1440×900, Chromium with ANGLE D3D11, CPU 1×, anonymous visitor. Heap measured after 3 forced GCs (HeapProfiler.collectGarbage). A control run without WebGL call wrapping (--bare) gives the same result.
steps: Open http://localhost:3200/ and hover the hero until the 3D is ready.
Scroll through the whole explode, open a part (e.g. turbina) and close it with Esc.
Click the header link „Delovi“ (/delovi, client-side), then use browser Back.
Repeat 4 times. After each step, run DevTools → Memory → Collect garbage and read Performance monitor → DOM Nodes, or take a heap snapshot and filter by „Detached“.
Scripted: `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-leak.mjs --gpu --cycles 4 --bare`; retaining paths: `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-retainers.mjs --gpu`.
findings.expected: After leaving the home page and a GC, nothing from an earlier home visit is reachable: no renderer, no canvas, no detached DOM (contract F8: dispose on unmount). DOM nodes and heap stay flat across cycles.
findings.actual: GPU resources are released: the context is lost, live contexts drop to 0 off the home page, and backing storage stays flat at 11.7 MB. But WebGL contexts reachable after GC grow 1→2→3→4→5 over 5 visits (WeakRef test). DOM nodes on /delovi grow 1365 → 2472 → 3579 (+1107 per home visit; bare run 1365 → 3055 → 4162 → 5269). Listeners grow by about 173 per visit and the JS heap by 0.7–1 MB per visit. Heap snapshot retaining paths: the latest renderer is held by React Three Fiber's module-level loop state (… .i .gl (WebGLRenderer) .domElement → canvas). Older renderers are held through a module-level three.js texture Source (RG half-float LUT, cache key "1001,1001,0,1006,1006,1,,1030,1016,false,false,false,1,"), used as a WeakMap key → .texture WebGLTexture → WebGL2RenderingContext → <canvas data-engine="three.js r186"> → the detached home tree.
findings.suggested_fix: components/three/canvas/HeroCanvas.tsx: capture gl in onCreated and call gl.dispose() on unmount, in addition to R3F's forceContextLoss. This releases WebGLTextures and the properties maps, so the module-level three texture's WeakMap entry stops pointing at the old WebGLTexture. Also dispose the PMREM render target explicitly, and clear scene.environment and heroStore.controller. Make sure R3F's module-level loop state does not keep the last root: upgrade R3F, or unmount through a path that clears it. Add a Playwright regression: 3 home ↔ /delovi cycles, forced GC, a WeakRef on the hero canvas must be empty and Performance.getMetrics Nodes must stay flat.
findings.standard: 3D-CONTRACT F8 (dispose on unmount); BRIEF §9 Reliability

verification.notes: verify-perf-3d-leak.mjs --gpu --cycles 3 (GL instrumentation on). DOM nodes on /delovi after a forced GC grow 1365 → 2472 → 3579 (+1107 per home visit, the same as the finder's figures). Reachable WebGL contexts grow 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 while live contexts go back to 0 off the home page. Listeners grow by about 174 and the heap by 0.8–1.1 MB per visit. GPU memory is released (0 MB off home). The retainer paths were not re-derived.

findings.title: High tier renders 4× MSAA at up to DPR 2: estimated GPU memory is 62 MB at DPR 1 and 114–194 MB on HiDPI screens, against a 60 MB budget
findings.context: Desktop 1440×900, high tier, DPR 1 and DPR 2 (HiDPI laptop), ANGLE D3D11, CPU 4×. GPU memory is estimated by instrumenting bufferData, texStorage2D, texImage2D and renderbufferStorage, plus the drawing buffer (RGBA8 + depth per sample × 4 samples + resolve).
steps: Run `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-frames.mjs --vp desktop --cpu 4 --gpu --runs 3 --dpr 2 --tag desktop-dpr2-cpu4-gpu` and read gl.perContext in the JSON.
Or in DevTools: document.querySelector('[data-testid=hero-track] canvas') → width/height, and getContext('webgl2').getContextAttributes().antialias.
findings.expected: 3D-CONTRACT F5: GPU memory ≤ 60 MB on desktop.
findings.actual: Resources are 20.7 MB (buffers 5.9 MB in 643 buffers, textures 14.8 MB in 13 textures) and would pass alone. The MSAA drawing buffer adds 41.3 MB at 1440×836 DPR 1, for 62.1 MB total. On a DPR 2 screen, after the adaptive step to 1.5 (2160×1254), it adds 93 MB for 113.7 MB total. Before that step, at 2880×1672, it is about 173 MB, or about 194 MB total. The cause is `antialias: tier === "high"` combined with `dpr={[1, 2]}`. Same numbers in 3/3 runs.
findings.suggested_fix: components/three/canvas/HeroCanvas.tsx: use MSAA only when the effective DPR is below 1.5 (antialias: tier === 'high' && window.devicePixelRatio < 1.5), or cap the high tier at DPR 1.5 when MSAA is on. At DPR 2 without MSAA the drawing buffer is about 38 MB, so the total is about 59 MB, and integrated GPUs (the typical high-tier laptop) get the fill-rate back. Also state in the contract whether the drawing buffer counts toward the budget.
findings.standard: 3D-CONTRACT F5 (GPU memory ≤ 60 MB)

verification.notes: GPU estimate at DPR 1 (1440×836) is 62.1 MB in 3 of 3 frames runs plus the leak run. At DPR 2, after the adaptive step to 1.5 (canvas 2160×1254), it is 113.7 MB. At 2880×1672 before that step, the drawing buffer alone works out to about 173 MB (4× MSAA color + depth + resolve). Cause confirmed in code: HeroCanvas.tsx sets antialias: tier === "high" with dpr={[1, TIER_MAX_DPR[tier]]}, and high is 2. The contract does not say whether the drawing buffer counts toward the 60 MB budget.

findings.title: Product titles drop the manufacturer before the brand suffix, so same-OEM parts from different makers get identical titles
findings.context: Any viewport, anonymous, server HTML
steps: curl each URL of a pair and compare the <title> values.
Compare their H1, manufacturer line and price: these are different products from different makers.
findings.expected: D193: „drop the brand suffix first, then the maker, then shorten the name“. That yields e.g. „Kočione pločice prednje, sa senzorom ATE 1K0 698 406 F“ vs „… Bosch 1K0 698 406 F“, so the titles stay unique.
findings.actual: Both products in each pair get the same <title> (3 duplicate pairs among 349 indexable URLs, e.g. twice „Kočioni di k prednji 312 × 25 mm, ventilirani 1K0 615 591 E“). productTitle() tries `name + code + suffix` before `name + maker + code`, so it drops the only differentiator (the maker) and keeps „ | SKLOP“. The suffix also appears on some product titles and not on others. A real VAG catalogue usually carries several makers per OEM number, so this will multiply.
evidence: docs/qa/audit/seo/crawl.csv (duplicate titles on the pairs above)
findings.suggested_fix: In lib/seo/templates.ts productTitle(), reorder the candidates to [name maker code suffix] → [name maker code] → [clamped name + maker + code] → [name code], matching D193. Add a uniqueness test over the products sitemap: no two active products may share a title.
findings.standard: SEO-ADS §J1 / D193; BRIEF §5 (unique titles)

verification.notes: I crawled all 349 sitemap URLs on :3100 with my own script. There are exactly 3 duplicate titles, and all 3 are the product pairs named in the finding (0009/e002 ATE vs Bosch, 0002/e001 Brembo vs ATE, 0057/e007 INA vs Gates). In each pair the JSON-LD brand, mpn and price differ. It is correct that productTitle() in lib/seo/templates.ts tries [name maker code suffix] → [name code suffix] → [name maker code] → [name code]. That drops the maker before the suffix, which contradicts D193. The finding overstates the cause and the fix, though. I simulated D193's own order with the real product names: only the brake-pad pair becomes unique („…sa senzorom ATE 1K0 698 406 F“, 54 characters). The disc pair (name + maker + code = 67–70 characters) and the timing-belt pair (61–63) still fall back to name + code, because D193 drops the maker before shortening the name. So 2 of the 3 duplicates come fr…
evidence: docs/qa/audit/verify/seo/seo-02-reproduce-simulation.txt (current order vs D193 order: D193 still duplicates the disc and timing-belt pairs)
curl /deo/kocioni-disk-prednji-312-25-mm-ventilirani-demo-0002 and -demo-e001 → both <title>Kočioni di k prednji 312 × 25 mm, ventilirani 1K0 615 591 E</title>; brand Brembo vs ATE
corrected_steps: curl -s http://localhost:3100/deo/kocione-plocice-prednje-sa-senzorom-demo-0009 and -demo-e002, then compare <title>: identical („… 1K0 698 406 F | SKLOP“); the JSON-LD brand is ATE vs Bosch.

The fix must clamp the name and keep the maker (update D193 to match), plus add a uniqueness test over the products sitemap.

findings.title: Out-of-range pagination (?strana=2…500) serves indexable, self-canonical copies of page 1
findings.context: Any viewport, anonymous, server HTML. The demo categories have at most 16 products, so every page ≥ 2 is out of range.
steps: curl -s "http://localhost:3100/delovi/kocioni-diskovi?strana=99" and read the status, robots meta, canonical and title.

Try ?strana=500 (lib/catalog/filters.ts MAX_PAGE).

Cause: listingIndexing() in lib/catalog/filters…

findings.title: Quantity steppers are 36 px (size="sm") everywhere a shopper or mechanic uses them; the design system specifies 44 px buttons
findings.area: Cart page, cart drawer, quick order, favorites (design-system conformance)
findings.context: Chromium, 360–2560, guest cart and mechanic
steps: Open /korpa at 390x844 with items.
Measure the „Smanji količinu“ and „Povećaj količinu“ buttons: 36x36 px. The quantity input is 56x34.
Open the cart drawer and /majstor/brza-porudzbina with results: same 36 px steppers, placed 4–8 px from the 44 px remove button.
findings.expected: DESIGN-SYSTEM §9.2: „Quantity stepper: [−] [ 2 ] [+] 44 px buttons“. §1.2 principle 5 and §5.2: primary touch targets are at least 44x44 px on phones.
findings.actual: Every stepper instance passes size="sm" (h-9 / size-9 = 36 px). On a phone in a workshop, the most-tapped control in the cart is below the system's own touch minimum. WCAG 2.5.8 (24 px) is still met.

verification.notes: Confirmed on the cart page and in the cart drawer at every width I tested (360, 390, 430, 768, 1440): the − and + buttons are 36x36 and the quantity input is 56x34, because CartView.tsx:131/150 pass size="sm" (h-9/size-9). That is also below the 8 px spacing rule in DESIGN-SYSTEM §5.2. FavoritesList.tsx:100 passes size="sm" in the source, but the account has no favorites, so nothing rendered to measure. The title's „everywhere“ is wrong: on the product page (/deo/...-demo-0004, 390x844) the stepper is 44x44 (AddToCartButton uses the md default). DESIGN-SYSTEM §9.7 also explicitly allows a „compact quantity stepper“ in mechanic portal list rows, and §5.2 allows dense 36 px in the portal on desktop. corrected_steps: Open /korpa with items at 390x844 (or any width from 360 to 1440): the „Smanji količinu“ and „Povećaj količinu“ buttons are 36x36 and the input is 56x34. The cart drawer is the same.

findings.title: Required fields are not exposed programmatically in checkout, inquiry and registration (only /prijava does it)
findings.route: /porudzbina (Ime, Prezime, Telefon, E-pošta), /upit (Opis, Ime, Telefon, consent), /registracija (all fields and consent)
findings.context: 1440x900 Chromium, accessibility tree
steps: Open /porudzbina with an item in the cart
Inspect #co-firstName, #co-lastName, #co-phone and #co-email for required or aria-required
Compare with /prijava
findings.expected: Mandatory controls carry aria-required="true" (or required), so screen readers announce „obavezno“ before the user hits an error. The visible convention of marking only optional fields „(nije obavezno)“ can stay.
findings.actual: req=- on every mandatory field in checkout, inquiry and registration. /prijava has required=true. Screen-reader users learn which fields are mandatory only from the error summary.
evidence: docs/qa/audit/a11y-store/forms-a.log (inq1440 fields req=-; auth /prijava req=true; /registracija req=-)
findings.suggested_fix: components/ui/Field.tsx already supports `required` in its context (lines 12/23/35). Default it to true when the field is not `optional`, and have Input, Textarea, Select and Checkbox emit aria-required.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (best practice)

verification.notes: Chromium at 1440x900.
