findings.title: Every signed-in page load forces a Convex Auth refresh (new JWT and rotated refresh token) although the JWT is valid for 1 h
findings.context: Chromium 1440×900, shared customer account, production build on :3100. Cookie values fingerprinted only (SHA-256 prefix).
steps: Run `node scripts/qa/audit/backend-session-refresh.mjs`: sign in, then 6 full page loads about 3 s apart.
__convexAuthJWT changed on 5 of 6 loads and __convexAuthRefreshToken on 5 of 6 (session-refresh.json).
Run `node scripts/qa/audit/backend-session-refresh-source.mjs`: each navigation issues a client fetch POST /api/auth that sets the new cookies (session-refresh-source.json).
The Convex log stream 16:19:32–16:23:08 shows 44 `auth:store type: refreshSession` against 4 sign-ins (convex-logs-stream.txt).
findings.expected: The server-provided JWT is reused. Refresh only happens in the last minute before the 1 h expiry (Convex Auth's own rule in the middleware).
findings.actual: One extra /api/auth round trip plus an auth:signIn action and refresh-token write for every page view of every signed-in user (mechanics are the heaviest users). The refresh-token chain grows per page view, and parallel tabs are more likely to hit reuse races.
findings.suggested_fix: Find out why the client calls fetchAccessToken({forceRefreshToken:true}) on load. Turn on `verbose` for ConvexAuthNextjsProvider/ConvexReactClient in a debug build (components/providers/ConvexClientProvider.tsx:18-28). Check that the token from ConvexAuthNextjsServerProvider (app/layout.tsx:54) reaches the client, and that the backend accepts the initial JWT (an AuthError, e.g. issuer mismatch, forces a refresh). Add an e2e assertion: at most one /api/auth POST across two navigations.
findings.standard: BRIEF §9 Reliability/Performance (no needless backend work per request), SECURITY §D1 (1 h JWT, refresh only near expiry)

verification.notes: Reproduced with my own script: Chromium 1440, shared customer account, :3100. Full document loads (page.goto /delovi, /korpa, /, /nalog): 4 of 4 each sent exactly one POST /api/auth {action:'auth:signIn', args:{refreshToken}}, and that response set a new __convexAuthJWT. Close variant, client-side Link navigation (/delovi, /nalog, /vozila, /; soft navigations, same timeOrigin): 0 of 4 sent POST /api/auth. So the refresh happens once per new page (entry, reload, new tab, hard navigation), not on every page view. The root cause is not a rejected JWT or an issuer mismatch, as the finding guessed. It is the Convex client's documented default in convex 1.46 authentication_manager.ts: '1. fetch a possibly cached token … 2. Immediately fetch a fresh token without using a cache'. When the server confirms the SSR-provided token, onTransition calls refetchToken() (forceRefreshToken: true) unless t…
evidence: docs/qa/audit/verify/backend/backend-08-reproduce.json (summary: apiAuthPostsDuringFullLoads 4 of 4, apiAuthPostsDuringClientNavs 0 of 4; each full load: POST /api/auth auth:signIn {refreshToken} then JWT cookie set)

docs/qa/audit/verify/backend/backend-08-reproduce-lib.txt (convex authentication_manager.ts:38-51 and 213-222, client.ts initialAuthTokenReuse docs, @convex-dev/auth client forceRefreshToken path, app client constructed without options)
corrected_steps: Run node scripts/qa/audit/verify-backend-08-refresh.mjs. It signs in the customer from .playwright/audit-accounts.json on http://localhost:3100 at 1440×900 in Chromium.

Phase A, full page loads of /delovi, /korpa, / and /nalog (3 s apart): each load sends one POST /api/auth with action auth:signIn and args {refreshToken}, and its response sets a new __convexAuthJWT (4 of 4).
Phase B, clicking in-page links to /delovi, /nalog, /vozila and / (soft navigations): no POST /api/auth (0 of 4).

Cause: the Convex client refetches the token right after the server confirms the SSR token (convex/src/browser/sync/authentication_manager.ts:213-220). Fix: new ConvexReactClient(url, { initialAuthTokenReuse: true }) in components/providers/ConvexClientProvider.tsx (experimental in convex 1.46, so pin it and cover it with an e2e test: at most one POST /api/auth across sign-in plus two reloads). findings.title: Desktop explode scroll at 4× CPU misses the documented WEB-QA smoothness bar: 290 draws per frame, and the X-ray two-pass recomputes program keys every frame
findings.context: Desktop 1440×900, DPR 1, high tier, ANGLE D3D11 (RTX 4060), CPU 4×, 60 wheel steps through the whole hero track. Mobile 390 @ 3×, mid tier, CPU 4× and 6×.
steps: Run `node scripts/qa/hero-frames.mjs --base http://localhost:3200 --cpu 4 --gpu` 3 times. This is the WEB-QA script, uninstrumented.
Run `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-frames.mjs --vp desktop --cpu 4 --gpu --runs 3` to get draws and triangles per frame, and `--vp mobile --cpu 6` for the low-end phone profile.
Run `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-profile.mjs --vp desktop --cpu 4 --gpu --phase scroll` for the CPU attribution.
findings.expected: docs/3d/WEB-QA.md §1: at 4× CPU, median 16.7 ms, p95 ≤ 33 ms and ≤ 6 % of frames over 33 ms (recorded as Pass). 3D-CONTRACT F5: 60 fps on desktop while scrubbing; draw calls ≤ 220 (desktop) and ≤ 150 (lite); lite ≤ 250 k triangles.
findings.actual: Uninstrumented desktop runs: p95 50.0 / 33.4 / 50.0 ms, frames over 33 ms 7.9 / 4.6 / 8.1 %, worst 83–100 ms, 10–21 long tasks. Instrumented runs: 8.8 / 8.4 / 16.4 %, p95 50–67 ms. So 5 of 6 runs miss the bar. At 1× the desktop is perfect (p95 16.7 ms, 0 %). Per frame: 290 draw calls and 416 k triangles on desktop (the GLB itself is 213 draws and 344 k), because the edges add hidden + depth + visible passes per shell mesh. Mobile: 172 draws and 257 k triangles per frame (lite budget 150 and 250 k). Mobile 4× passes (1.3–4.6 %), but mobile 6× has 21.8 / 32.6 / 25.1 % of frames over 33 ms (p95 67–100 ms). CPU profile at 4×: the main thread is busy 5.37 s out of 9.91 s, and three's render takes 73 % of that. getParameters (390 ms) + getProgramCacheKey (116 ms) of self time come from X-ray materials that use transparent + DoubleSide: three's automatic two-pass sets material.needsUpdate = true twice per object per frame.
findings.suggested_fix: components/three/canvas/materials.ts createXrayMaterial: replace side: DoubleSide and three's automatic two-pass with two explicit materials: BackSide at 0.5× alpha rendered first through renderOrder, then FrontSide. Alternatively use forceSinglePass plus a back-face clone. Either way needsUpdate is never set per frame. components/three/canvas/enhance.ts: stop adding 3 draws per shell mesh. Precompute the edge lines in the pipeline as one line primitive per part node, and drop the separate depth pre-pass by letting the front-face shell pass write depth for the visible-edge test. Re-measure with hero-frames.mjs and correct docs/3d/WEB-QA.md §1.
findings.standard: 3D-CONTRACT F5 (runtime 60 fps desktop while scrubbing; draw-call and lite triangle budgets); docs/3d/WEB-QA.md §1 scroll smoothness bar

verification.notes: The smoothness-bar miss did not reproduce. Desktop 4× on the RTX 4060: instrumented runs p95 33.3/33.3/33.4 ms with 0.7/1.5/6.8 % of frames over 33 ms; uninstrumented hero-frames.mjs p95 33.4/33.3 ms with 4.3/1.5 %. So 4 of 5 runs meet the ≤ 6 % bar, against the finder's 5 of 6 misses. Mobile 4×: 2.3–6.6 % instrumented, 0.7/5.5 % uninstrumented. The per-frame counts are confirmed: desktop 290 draws and 416,272 triangles, mobile 172 draws and 257,044 triangles, against the F5 figures of 220 and 150 draws and the lite 250 k triangles. Those budgets are defined for the GLB after merging, which is 213 draws, so how runtime passes count against them is open to interpretation. I did not re-measure mobile 6× or the getProgramCacheKey profile.
corrected_steps: node scripts/qa/hero-frames.mjs --base http://localhost:3200 --cpu 4 --gpu, 2 or more times on a quiet machine: p95 is about 33.3 ms and 1.5–4.3 % of frames are over 33 ms (the bar is met).
Record draws and triangles per frame with verify-perf-3d-frames.mjs: 290 and 416 k on desktop, 172 and 257 k on mobile.

findings.title: Software WebGL (SwiftShader, llvmpipe, blocklisted GPUs, VMs/RDP) gets the full high tier: p95 about 1 s per frame, worst about 2 s
findings.context: Desktop 1440×900 in Chromium with software GL (--use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader), CPU 1× and 4×. This stands in for a VM or RDP session, a blocklisted GPU, or Linux without GPU drivers.
steps: Run `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-frames.mjs --vp desktop --cpu 1 --runs 2 --tag desktop-cpu1-swiftshader` and `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-frames.mjs --vp desktop --cpu 4 --runs 3`.

The adaptive DPR is already at 1, so it cannot help.

Add a runtime watchdog in HeroCanvas.tsx: if the median frame is over 50 ms across the first 60 continuous frames at DPR 1, set status 'failed' so the existing posters take over. verification.notes: With --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader at 1×, the tier is 'high': p95 1117 ms, p99 1400 ms, worst 1900 ms, 39.7 % of frames over 33 ms. lib/three/tier.ts:57 probes with failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat: false and never checks the renderer. Exposure is narrower than claimed: the repro needs --enable-unsafe-swiftshader, which recent Chrome requires for SwiftShader WebGL.
